subject: ArrTags release candidate 0.1.0 (HEAD 0ab5f23; installed artifact artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip sha256 bd10b9b6bf5d31049082d27625b18ba127eb6e2860a454fe2d3c35ccebaaee51)

findings.area: webhook HTTP boundary / input handling (authenticate-before-body and payload bound)
findings.description: The anonymous webhook actions ([ApiController] ArrTagsWebhookController.ReceiveSonarrAsync/ReceiveRadarrAsync, CancellationToken-only parameters) cause ASP.NET Core MVC model binding to run the form value-provider factory, which reads/parses the request body BEFORE the action's shared-secret check for form content types (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data). Reproduced live: with those content types, a request carrying NO or an invalid secret is answered by the framework's form/model-state processing (HTTP 400) instead of the uniform 401, and the body is read up to Kestrel's 30,000,000-byte cap pre-authentication; the configured OperationalLimits.WebhookMaxPayloadBytes (default 262,144 B) is therefore NOT the effective bound on that path. For application/json (and absent/text content types) the shipped ordering holds: an oversized JSON body with no secret returns 401 before the plugin reads any body, and an authenticated oversized JSON body returns 413 via WebhookBodyReader. Impact: no credential, header, body, or configuration detail is exposed; no plugin work occurs pre-auth (no reconciliation, provider call, or artwork mutation); the concrete consequence is a pre-authentication resource-consumption amplification (~30 MB read/buffered plus multipart/urlencoded parsing per unauthenticated request versus the documented 256 KiB bound) and a real deviation from the ADR-012 / architecture contract that the boundary 'authenticates first, then enforces the bounded payload limit'. The read remains finite because Kestrel's global MaxRequestBodySize (30 MB) and the framework form limits (ValueLengthLimit 4 MB, KeyLengthLimit 2048, MultipartBodyLengthLimit 128 MB) still apply. Classified MEDIUM rather than HIGH because it is a bounded host-enforced amplification and a contract/hardening gap, not a credential exposure, auth bypass that grants plugin work, or data-integrity loss.

findings.recommended_action: Ensure the anonymous webhook route does not process non-JSON request bodies before model binding: reject unsupported content types before any body read (for example an explicit supported-content-type constraint returning 415) or disable automatic form value-provider/model binding for these actions, so authentication and the configured WebhookMaxPayloadBytes bound strictly precede any body read. Add a regression test asserting 401 for an unauthenticated oversized form/multipart body and that the configured bound (not the framework/Kestrel default) governs the webhook path.

findings.description: When IPluginManager is unavailable or the loaded plugin instance cannot be found, CreateStateRepository roots the entire authoritative plugin state at Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags"). On a shared host that is a predictable, world-accessible location; if this fallback ever engaged it would place authoritative artwork/provenance/operation state (and its quarantine area) under a shared temp path where another local user could pre-create or observe a same-named directory. It is not triggered on the pinned host (Plugin is found and DataFolderPath is ProgramDataPath/ArrTags), and it is not remotely reachable.
evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:174-183 (string.IsNullOrEmpty(plugin?.DataFolderPath) ? Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags") : plugin!.DataFolderPath)
src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs:69-73 (normal state root is ProgramDataPath/ArrTags; verified live: /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags was not created and no PluginsPath/ArrTags orphan exists)
findings.recommended_action: Fail closed (do not register state-dependent services) or use a host-private directory when the plugin data folder cannot be resolved, instead of a shared temp path.

findings.description: The versioned state envelope's SHA-256 (PayloadSha256) covers only PayloadJson. Envelope metadata (SchemaVersion, Kind, RecordId, Authority, Terminal, UpdatedUtc) is not covered by the hash. In particular retention decisions trust the unauthenticated Terminal and UpdatedUtc fields, so a writer able to modify state files could make an authoritative record eligible for pruning without invalidating the integrity check. This is not an escalation because local write access to the state root is already the administrative boundary and such a writer can delete files directly; it bounds the guarantee to 'detects accidental tearing/corruption', not 'authenticates a malicious writer'.
evidence: src/ArrTags/State/StateEnvelopeCodec.cs:83-113 (hash compared only against parsed.PayloadJson), :123-154 (metadata parsed without integrity coverage)
src/ArrTags/State/StateEnvelope.cs (Terminal/UpdatedUtc are envelope fields)
src/ArrTags/State/StateRetention.cs:154-165 (retention reads envelope.Terminal/envelope.UpdatedUtc)
findings.recommended_action: None required for the release; optionally cover the envelope metadata in the integrity hash or document that StateEnvelopeCodec is a corruption detector rather than a tamper MAC.

findings.description: Unauthenticated webhook failures return ASP.NET Core application/problem+json bodies that reflect framework/pipeline detail (for example 'The max request body size is 30000000 bytes', 'Form key length limit 2048 exceeded', 'Multipart header length limit 16384 exceeded') plus a trace id. No secret, header, candidate, body, plugin, route, or item existence detail is reflected. This is the same class as the already-documented D1 (401 body vs ADR-012 'no body'), extended to the form-driven 400 paths.

docs/limitations.md D1
findings.recommended_action: None required; optionally normalise error responses to a minimal body if desired.

findings.description: The Sonarr/Radarr API keys and the inbound webhook shared secret are persisted only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML (data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml) and are returned by Jellyfin's authenticated, elevation-gated plugin-configuration API to administrators. This matches the accepted ADR-005 single-source-of-truth design (protection at rest follows Jellyfin's data-folder permissions and administrative boundary; ArrTags adds no second secret store). Independent checks found the values in no other live location.

findings.description: Re-confirmed accepted limitation D2: ArtworkSubjectGate.Gates is a process-lifetime static ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> with no eviction. Growth is keyed by (Jellyfin item id, image surface), which is not attacker-controllable and is bounded in practice by the host's distinct library items; it is not a log, HTTP, or persisted-state path. No attacker-influenced unbounded collection was found elsewhere: WebhookIntake (capacity 256), WebhookCoalescingWindow (4x intake), LibraryWorkQueue (QueueCapacity, default 512), MetadataStateStore.Enumerate and WebhookReconciliationResolver (ReconciliationBatchSize, max 1000), provider response reads (ProviderResponseLimitBytes, default 8 MiB), source/derived artifact reads/writes (32 MiB), decoded dimensions (8192/side), JSON depth (16) and Sonarr episode entries (32) are all explicitly bounded.

summary: Independent adversarial audit of ArrTags 0.1.0 (HEAD 0ab5f23; frozen artifact sha256 bd10b9b6bf5d31049082d27625b18ba127eb6e2860a454fe2d3c35ccebaaee51) found no open BLOCKER or HIGH. Secrets are structurally contained: no logging exists at all in the plugin; SecretLease never exposes/prints its value, clears it on Dispose, applies API keys only as X-Api-Key headers, and is version-matched and fail-closed; the public configuration snapshot carries only has-API-key booleans; fingerprints, cache keys, canonical state, queue items, and operation/error records contain no secret. Live checks found the configured keys/secret only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML (accepted ADR-005 design). The webhook route authenticates before plugin work, uses a bounded constant-time compare (1024-char candidate), fails closed with a uniform 401, and bounds/persists nothing from the payload; the item-image read route is explicitly not treated as an authorization boundary. State integrity is strong: atomic flushed writes, versioned SHA-256-tagged envelopes, traversion-safe single-segment ids and 64-char hash artifact ids, cache-discard vs authoritative-quarantine split, generation/phase fencing, a durable write-ahead publication journal with fence re-reads before mutation and before commit, and fail-closed artifact GC. Provider integration is GET-only. All queues, retries, response/artifact sizes, decoded dimensions, JSON depth, and concurrency are explicitly bounded, and no attacker-influenced unbounded in-memory collection was found. One new MEDIUM (SEC-1) was reproduced on the pinned host: for form content types (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data) ASP.NET Core [ApiController] model binding reads/parses the request body before the action authenticates and before the configured 256 KiB WebhookMaxPayloadBytes bound applies, allowing an unauthenticated client to force up to Kestrel's 30 MB per-request pre-auth body read/parse (HTTP 400 instead of 401). It is a bounded, host-enforced resource-consumption and documented-contract gap (no credential exposure, no plugin work, no integrity loss), classified MEDIUM and recommended for a tracked fix before or shortly after release. Remaining items are LOW (state-root temp fallback, SEC-2) or INFORMATIONAL (unauthenticated envelope metadata in the integrity scope, framework detail in error bodies, accepted secrets-at-rest design, accepted ArtworkSubjectGate bound). reviewer_status APPROVED: no open BLOCKER/HIGH.
